records.region: Western Nevada, Lodi-side valleys and Gabbs Valley
records.candidate_name_role: No representative natural-river name established for the entire canyon, alluvial floor, lower wash and playa composite.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: Gabbs Wash is supported only for the lower receiving reach. No whole natural-river name is established for the long unnamed opening, alluvial floor and terminal Gabbs Valley playa composite.
records.completion_scope: Full selected ordinary geographic correspondence completed. Null whole-feature naming is a scope limit, not a missing geographic through-link. No further source expansion is needed.

scope_limits: No single natural-river name is established over the entire modeled composite; Gabbs Wash is retained as a bounded lower-reach name.

The selected upper and middle valley-floor passages lack a continuous blue stream line. Continuous mapped canyon and alluvial-floor correspondence is sufficient for this ordinary geographic assessment; present surface flow is unverified.
The playa is read as a receiving setting, not a currently inundated lake or evidence of an exact active channel.
No formal name register, precise name boundary, exact bank alignment or Korean name was verified.

bounded_name_observations.name: Gabbs Wash
bounded_name_observations.scope: Directly labeled lower receiving corridor, principally stored parts15–18. The separately mapped western upper Gabbs Wash branch is not the selected opening.

bounded_name_observations.name: Lodi Valley
bounded_name_observations.scope: Selected upper-middle alluvial receiving setting; not a whole-feature hydronym.

bounded_name_observations.name: Gabbs Valley
bounded_name_observations.scope: Western terminal receiving floor; not a lake or river name.

records.candidate_name_role: No whole natural-river representative established; named draws and Laguna del Perro are bounded landform and terminal-playa observations only.
records.material_pending_reason: The selected opening, named-draw surroundings, broad Moriarty–Estancia receiving floor and Laguna del Perro terminal are mapped. Full correspondence remains unestablished at the small-depression exit near Stinking Spring and, especially, the transfer from the separate northeastern playa across intervening ground into Laguna del Perro. These are lake/depression-to-receiver gaps rather than a demand for an exactly wet blue line. One source-material-pending primary state; no whole river candidate is assigned.
records.completion_scope: Bounded pass finished with concrete selected through-link gaps. No additional source expansion was made after the terminal view. One source-material-pending primary classification; no additional access-pending or completed name-scope classification.

scope_limits: The whole natural-river name remains unsupported; bounded draw names do not establish a single representative hydronym.

The small depression near Stinking Spring and the separate northeastern playa are geographically located, but their selected onward transfers require additional source support. The finding does not assert that those connections are physically impossible.
The mapped long Laguna del Perro floor is continuous within the selected terminal section. This does not establish a present water surface or perennial flow.
No formal registry, current water-management operation, exact bank or Korean rendering was verified.

bounded_name_observations.name: Bachelor Draw

bounded_name_observations.name: Buffalo Draw

bounded_name_observations.name: Salt Draw
bounded_name_observations.scope: Lower-middle receiving-floor setting north of the playa complex.

bounded_name_observations.name: Laguna del Perro
bounded_name_observations.scope: Directly labeled long receiving playa, including selected parts18–20 and the coincident source/render endings. Not a river name.

records.region: Southeastern Nicaragua, Río Indio drainage and Caribbean coastal plain north of Greytown
records.candidate_name_role: Representative receiving-system identity, not a scalar name for every selected headward tributary, wetland channel or marine ending.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected unnamed western feeder joins the mapped Río Indio receiving corridor. Its eastward trunk and lower coastal channel correspond to that drainage; the generalized terminal reaches the adjacent Caribbean receiving coast before the separately mapped southward outlet route near Greytown.
records.completion_scope: Original INETER/ANA/UNI/GIZ-PROATAS atlas cartography and three completed, inspected World Imagery views support Río Indio as the representative receiving system. All 43 stored parts, the western feeder-to-trunk join, fragment join, lower wetland course, and separate source/render endings were reviewed. The offshore terminal is a generalized coastal extension; it is not evidence of a direct river mouth through the beach barrier at that point.
records.supported_name_scope: The selected unnamed western feeder joins the mapped Río Indio receiving corridor. Its eastward trunk and lower coastal channel correspond to that drainage; the generalized terminal reaches the adjacent Caribbean receiving coast before the separately mapped southward outlet route near Greytown.

scope_limits: The selected western feeder has no supported separate hydronym in the inspected sources; Río Indio is a representative receiving-system identity only.

The selection terminates on a generalized path toward the adjacent sea rather than following the entire mapped coast-parallel lower Indio to its southern mouth. Source and render endpoints were not equated with a surveyed natural river mouth.
No present river-mouth opening, channel activity, imagery date, flow direction at individual side channels or precise wet-season hydraulics is asserted.

The original private restriction ledger is incomplete. Lack of a local match was not treated as permission; actual project identities and underlying mapping relationships were distinguished before requests.

bounded_name_observations.name: Río Indio
bounded_name_observations.scope: Atlas Map 5 labels the coastal-parallel receiving course Indio; its connected drainage supports the representative identity. The western chosen feeder is not separately named in the inspected map.

bounded_name_observations.name: Indian River
bounded_name_observations.scope: Incer printed page 22 explicitly discusses Indio as the Spanish form of historical English Indian River. This is authorial historical naming context, not a contemporary official-register alias or a new reading of the old Admiralty maps he mentions.

bounded_name_observations.name: Mar Caribe
bounded_name_observations.scope: The atlas and imagery establish the Caribbean coastal receiving setting; this sea name is not an alias for the river.

bounded_name_observations.name: Greytown / San Juan de Nicaragua; Bahía San Juan de Nicaragua
bounded_name_observations.scope: Atlas labels for the southern coastal outlet setting. These places are downstream contextual references, not names for the selected river or its rendered endpoint.

records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The inspected source is unlabelled photographic imagery. It supports the complete alluvial/playa-to-shallow-water geography, but supplies no whole-feature natural-river name or representative receiving-system hydronym. The stopped optional hydrological report supplies no new evidence.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Baja California hydro-system70756810 has complete ordinary geographic correspondence across all 24 selected parts: an open alluvial-plain beginning,westward mountain-toe turn,northwestern piedmont corridor and broad playa approach ending inside a shallow-water basin. The unlabelled imagery does not establish a representative natural-river name,so the result is a completed null naming-scope hold. Accepted,scalar and Korean names remain null; no registry verification or product application is claimed.
records.completion_scope: The complete selected opening, every one of the24 stored parts, their transitions, common alluvial receiving corridors, side-fan joins, broad northern playa approach and actual selected terminal setting were read on one complete original photographic overview and native-size local excerpts. The actual export extent was subsequently confirmed with the same view parameters. The ordinary geographic corridor is continuous; narrower photographed channel offsets do not create an unsupported interbasin connection. No natural-river name or named representative receiving identity was established.

scope_limits: No representative natural-river name,alias or Korean form is supported by the actually inspected photographic source.
The selected line is generalized and sometimes occupies broad alluvial or playa floor beside a narrow visible channel. This finding establishes ordinary geographic correspondence only.
A photographed waterbody at the ending is not proof of a perennial lake or its complete modern extent. Scene dates and current flow are unverified.
Nearby other river channels,larger western wash and mountain massifs remain unnamed and are not imported as candidate identities.
The historic private restriction ledger remains incomplete. The new exact INEGI refusal remains controlling despite earlier normally read independent-publication evidence.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
